Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
506 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
High Wind Watch and Storm Watch have both been upgraded to Warnings. 
The Wind Advisory now includes Western Passaic County.

For Thanksgiving, Coastal Flood Warnings have been issued for 
the entire coastline except for southeast CT. For Friday, a 
Coastal Flood Watch remains for much of the coastline for the 
daytime high tide cycle. A Coastal Flood Advisory remains in 
effect for southeast CT for Thanksgiving and Friday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) A storm system impacts the area Thanksgiving into Friday 
with rain and strong to damaging winds.

2) Widespread moderate coastal flooding likely for the 
Thanksgiving AM and PM high tides, with minor to moderate 
impacts for the Friday AM high tide. In addition, widespread 
beach flooding and dune erosion expected along the open water 
shorelines during the times of high tide, with localized 
overwashes possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
The Thanksgiving storm is still on track, with the bulk of the rain 
and wind impacts most likely in the afternoon and evening. 

There remains some model uncertainty with regard to timing, so
the window for peak storm impacts remains roughly 10am through 
the overnight. However, this window in reality should be a bit 
smaller, as the heavy rain and strong winds are cut short by the
dry slot blasting thru from the south. Based on latest model 
trends, the end time of both the Wind Advisory and High Wind 
Warning may be able to be trimmed back by a few hours. Not 
enough confidence to do this right now due to a lack of solid
agreement among the models.

The strongest winds are currently anticipated during Thursday 
afternoon and evening, which is when a strong low level jet and 
tight pressure gradient coincide. Gusts up to around 60 mph are 
anticipated in the Warned area with 45-55 mph gusts in the 
Advisory area, which now includes Western Passaic County after 
collaboration with WFO PHI. 

Rainfall amounts have increased from the previous forecast. The 
heaviest rainfall appears to be most likely during Thursday evening 
when strong upward forcing from the low level jet interacts with an 
anomalously moist airmass for this time of the year. In addition, 
there is the possibility of a rumble of thunder with some models 
showing some elevated CAPE during the time of the strong lift from 
the LLJ. There's enough of a signal by some of the CAMs that there's 
at least a slight chance that 1" per hour rainfall rates pass 
through the vicinity of NYC Metro, with SPC now including a Slight 
Risk of flash flooding for this area during Thursday. The flash 
flooding threat appears to be limited to urbanized areas as FFG 
values elsewhere are high due to relatively dry conditions lately, 
and a Marginal Risk for flash flooding remains in place for 
these spots. For the entire forecast area, minor/poor drainage 
flooding is the more likely scenario.

The rain gets cut off by the dry slot in the eve, again the timing 
will be refined as we get closer, with  some lingering light rain or 
dz under the residual stratus deck overnight into Friday morning. An 
upper low and cold pool aloft come through on Fri afternoon. This 
could spark a few showers, with rainfall on the light side.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
With a recent full moon, astronomical tides remain rather high and 
many locations need less than a foot to reach minor coastal flood 
benchmarks with the AM high tides, but closer to 2 ft with the PM 
high tides.

Minor coastal flooding is expected with this morning's high tide for 
southern Nassau county communities, elsewhere localized minor 
coastal flooding or no coastal flooding.

A period of gale to storm force ENE winds will affect the region 
Thursday morning into Thursday Night. The region remains between an 
approaching low pressure and strong high pressure to the north. This 
will bring the likelihood for widespread moderate coastal flooding 
with the Thursday AM and PM high tides, with potential for major 
coastal flooding along the western Great South bay. Other areas of 
notes for significant impacts will be the Peconic Bay area with 
funneling of surge towards the Peconic River, and along W LI Sound 
shoreline with moderate water levels combined with high wave action. 
Surge up the tidally affected rivers (Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic 
will result in minor to moderate flooding as well.

The Thursday AM high tide is the higher high tide by at least 1 ft, 
but the peak surge will likely occur Thursday afternoon into 
evening, based on a multi-model mean of peak winds occurring Thu 
aft/eve. This may result in similar water levels for both tidal 
cycles for much of the area. The forecast has been leaned to a blend 
of 75th percentile of Stevens SFAS and NAEFS P-ETSS (good 
middle ground btwn ECMWF and GEFS PETSS) with deterministic 
ETSS/STOFS. The lean towards the higher end water level scenario
to provide a bit of safety margin, if the timing of strongest 
winds is quicker than currently forecast and with expectation of
winds increasing thru the time of high tide Thu AM.

For the Friday AM high tides, winds switch to the southwest. 
Potential for another round of moderate coastal flooding for the 
southern bays of LI and Queens, particularly for the eastern Great 
South Bay. Elsewhere, offshore flow should allow for water to drain 
out of more open water location (LIS and NY/NJ Harbor) resulting in 
minor coastal flood impacts. 

For the oceanfront, breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result in 
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of high 
tide. There is potential for localized overwashes, exacerbating 
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective 
dunes. Along Western LI Sound and Twin Forks, breaking waves of 3 to 
6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. 
Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable 
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential 
for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well.

Heavy rain coinciding with the Thursday evening high tides could 
exacerbate street flooding issues along the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /10Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
High pressure will be in control through this evening as it moves 
across to the north.

VFR conditions through this evening. MVFR ceilings develop for the 
city and southern coastal terminals towards and after 06z Thu. 

Winds N to NE around 10 kt or less early this morning. Winds shift 
to the ENE settle in at 7 to 12 kt for much of the day.

     NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

No amendments expected.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Thursday through Sunday... 

Late Wednesday night: VFR gives way to MVFR towards and after 06z. Winds
increase, especially towards the morning push.

Thanksgiving: IFR conditions in rain develop. E winds 15-25kt G30-40kt.
Peak gusts potentially higher. LLWS possible with 50+kt at 1000ft.

Friday: VFR and pockets of MVFR. W winds gusting to 25-35 kt. 

Saturday: MVFR possible with W winds gusting to 20-30 kt.

Sunday: VFR. SW winds 5-10 kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Storm Watches have been converted to Warnings on all waters 
with enough confidence in the occurrence of at least 50kt gusts
during the daytime on Thursday and into the first half of the 
night. A long enough period of Gales precedes this tonight to 
warrant a Gale Warning leading up to the Storm Warning. Seas on 
the ocean are modeled to build to around 20ft at the height of 
the storm in the late aftn and eve, with waves on the Sound and 
the NY Harbor entrance up to around 10ft.

Conditions improve a little on Fri, but a SW gale is likely on 
the ocean and maybe on some of the non-ocean waters as well.  
Winds diminish to SCA lvls on Sat, and likely blw SCA lvls on 
Sun.
